questions.q: How was time measured through history, and how does a pendulum help?
answer: Time has always been measured by using events that repeat regularly.

answer.text: People first used natural repeating events such as day and night, the phases of the Moon and the seasons. Later they built devices like the sundial, the water clock and the sand clock or hourglass.

Galileo noticed that a simple pendulum — a bob hung by a thread — swings to and fro with a steady rhythm. One complete to-and-fro swing is an oscillation, and the time for one oscillation, the time period, is constant for a given pendulum. This steady time period made pendulum clocks possible.
Modern clocks use quartz for great accuracy, and the SI unit of time is the second.

questions.q: Define speed, and explain how a distance–time graph shows different kinds of motion.

answer.text: Speed is the distance travelled in a unit of time, found by dividing distance by time. Its SI unit is the metre per second, though vehicle speeds are often given in kilometres per hour. A speedometer shows a vehicle's speed and an odometer the distance travelled.

In such a graph, time is plotted on the horizontal axis and distance on the vertical axis. A straight sloping line shows uniform motion, in which equal distances are covered in equal times. A horizontal line shows that the object is at rest, since its distance does not change. A curved line shows non-uniform motion, and the steeper the line, the greater the speed.
